Messages.Author: Harry Smith
Messages.Body:
I was playing a game o jyhad where my predator was a Malkavian S&B deck.
I was playing my Tremere Intercept, having fun blocking his foolish
attempts at stealth. Then he pulls out Blood Bond, and plays it against
my best blocker (Cassandra w/ Sport Bike). I was tapped at the time and
unable to block. I don't personally have a Blood Bond and have never
before had one used on me, so I was quite suprised when I discover than
Cassandra can never again block Leandro (+2 bleed, sup dom (skill card),
sup obf). He promptly pulled off a +2 stealth 9 bleed (Leandro w/ Govern
the Unaglined, Conditioning, and Lost in Crowds), and I went under. The
point of this is: is there anything that can be done about Blood Bond after
it's been played? With the Incriminating Video Tape, it can be stolen
or destroyed, but it looks like the only way to get rid of Blood Bond is
to kill the vamp (not easy to kill Leandro when he's got a handfull of
Read Intentions).

Messages.Author: Nicole Janine Purvis
Messages.Body:
Harry Smith (hsm...@garfield.msms.doe.k12.ms.us) wrote:
: I was playing a game o jyhad where my predator was a Malkavian S&B deck.



Nothing can be done about the Blood Bond; the fact that it cannot be
stolen is a double-edged sword: only the person who put it on that vamp
cannot be blocked by that vamp... So in this case, only Cassandra could
not block Leandro, whereas, with an incriminating videotape, the opponent
could swap it around [either by movement actions, or by Heidelburg
Castle] and make several of his minions unblockable by Cassandra...

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
hi...@mail.utexas.edu (Stephen Beaulieu) writes:

>In article <DLDI3...@news.research.kpn.com>, Joost Hage
><ha...@cs.utwente.nl> wrote:

>: Doesn't the Heidelburg Castle enable you to swap all CARDS between your

>: vamps? Doesn't this also meen you can swap the Blood Bond (and retainers)
>: after all?
>:
>: Just a thought, Joost

>No, Heidelburg Castle allows the swapping of equipment, retainers, and

>blood only between 2 vamps you control.

>Sorry, no moving blood bond.

Correct, and Blood Bond couldn't be moved even if Heidelburg did allow
you to move arbitrary cards, since Blood Bond is not played *on* the
vampire, but merely names (targets) the vampire.
